negative_action: Using persuasion or lecturing to challenge patient thoughts
description: Attempting to change patient beliefs through debate, persuasion, or didactic explanation rather than guided discovery.
risk: Can foster resistance, damage the therapeutic alliance, and reduce patient engagement.

negative_action: Ignoring patient reality or advocating uncritical positivity
description: Encouraging patients to adopt overly positive viewpoints without considering their experiences or context.
risk: Risk of invalidating patient experiences and eroding trust in the therapist.

negative_action: Rigid application of techniques
description: Using CBT methods without individual adaptation or ongoing feedback.
risk: Decreases effectiveness and may alienate the patient.

negative_action: Neglecting the therapeutic alliance
description: Failing to establish, maintain, or repair a strong therapeutic relationship.
risk: Weakens patient engagement and reduces likelihood of positive outcomes.

negative_action: Making premature inferences or assumptions
description: Drawing conclusions about patient experiences or problems without sufficient evidence or collaboration.
risk: Leads to mistakes in conceptualization and reduced patient collaboration.

negative_action: Focusing excessively on the past without cause
description: Dwelling on past events not directly relevant to current issues or alliance ruptures.
risk: Can divert from present-focused CBT work and reduce session effectiveness.

negative_action: Delivering treatment in an impersonal or rote manner
description: Using a cold, scripted, or unengaged approach in sessions.
risk: Can make patients feel undervalued and impair the therapeutic alliance.

negative_action: Ignoring patient feedback
description: Failing to attend or respond to negative feedback from the patient.
risk: Reduces trust and engagement; hinders collaborative work.

negative_action: Assigning generic interventions or homework
description: Providing unpersonalized tasks or interventions regardless of patient needs.
risk: Can reduce relevance, adherence, and patient motivation.

negative_action: Questioning or challenging core beliefs prematurely
description: Addressing deeply held beliefs before the patient is ready.
risk: Can threaten the alliance and reduce therapeutic credibility.

negative_action: Interpreting data without patient input
description: Making therapeutic interpretations or inferences without basing them on patient data.
risk: Can lead to misunderstanding and rupture trust.

negative_action: Misattributing organic causes as psychological
description: Assuming psychological explanations without ruling out medical factors.
risk: Medical issues may go untreated and worsen problem.

negative_action: Over-focusing on negatives
description: Concentrating solely on patients' difficulties rather than strengths.
risk: May undermine hope and motivation.

negative_action: Pushing patients to reveal sensitive material before readiness
description: Encouraging premature disclosure of distressing information.
risk: Can cause increased distress and potentially retraumatize clients.

negative_action: Using stigmatizing diagnostic labels
description: Labeling patients with terms like 'personality disorder' in a stigmatizing fashion.
risk: Can damage the therapeutic relationship and reinforce shame.

negative_action: Dictating the session agenda
description: Exercising excessive control over what is discussed in session.
risk: Undermines collaboration and patient engagement.

negative_action: Assigning homework without collaboration or ensuring feasibility
description: Providing tasks without discussing practicality or getting patient buy-in.
risk: Decreases adherence and may foster feelings of failure.

negative_action: Overloading severely depressed or inactive patients
description: Setting up overly ambitious or packed activity schedules.
risk: Can lead to overwhelming the patient and reduce chances of success.

negative_action: Focusing only on activity quantity
description: Prioritizing number of tasks over quality (mastery or pleasure).
risk: Reduces the therapeutic benefit and motivation from activities.

negative_action: Forcing cognitive strategies during high distress
description: Requiring cognitive tasks when emotional arousal or executive function is impaired.
risk: Can increase frustration and sense of inadequacy.

negative_action: Pushing patients to compare themselves to prior functioning
description: Encouraging comparisons to their non-depressed or 'best' self.
risk: Can lower self-esteem and motivation.

negative_action: Pushing cognitive restructuring when the alliance or readiness is weak or distress is high
description: Attempting restructuring interventions without established rapport or if the patient is overwhelmed.
risk: Can lead to disengagement and potential alliance rupture.

negative_action: Overemphasizing worksheet completion
description: Insisting on completing all forms and questions regardless of utility.
risk: Can create patient frustration and feelings of inadequacy.

negative_action: Invalidating emotional experiences or the significance of imagery
description: Minimizing, criticizing, or pathologizing patients' imagery or emotions even if they seem unrealistic.
risk: May hinder trust and impede emotional processing.

negative_action: Treating core beliefs as facts
description: Reinforcing or failing to question maladaptive core beliefs.
risk: Maintains dysfunctional thought patterns and prolongs symptoms.

negative_action: Premature attribution of failures to internal causes
description: Attributing setbacks or failures to internal traits like incompetence without considering alternatives.
risk: Can reinforce negative self-concept and impede progress.

negative_action: Allowing excessive distraction from emotion
description: Permitting patients to consistently avoid emotional experience through distraction.
risk: Hinders learning and prevents emotional processing.

negative_action: Making homework assignments too difficult or ill-defined
description: Assigning tasks that outpace readiness or are not specific enough.
risk: Leads to noncompliance and feelings of failure.

negative_action: Shaming or criticizing patients for lack of homework completion
description: Using punitive or negative feedback for incomplete assignments.
risk: Reduces motivation, increases shame, and undermines collaboration.

negative_action: Fostering dependence on the therapist
description: Positioning oneself as responsible for solving all patient problems.
risk: Prevents patient autonomy and self-efficacy.

negative_action: Ignoring or minimizing termination-related anxieties
description: Failing to address patient fears or concerns about ending therapy.
risk: Can lead to unresolved dependency, distress, or unfinished therapeutic work.

negative_action: Pursuing topics that activate painful core beliefs without readiness
description: Addressing distressing topics or beliefs before the patient is prepared.
risk: May cause increased distress and damage alliance.

negative_action: Rigid adherence to standard format or agenda
description: Following a set structure without considering individual patient needs.
risk: Reduces patient engagement and treatment effectiveness.

negative_action: Assigning blame to patient or therapist for problems
description: Focusing on fault-finding rather than collaborative problem-solving.
risk: Undermines the therapeutic relationship and progress.

negative_action: Practicing CBT tools without personal experience
description: Using or assigning CBT interventions without firsthand practice or understanding obstacles.
risk: May reduce empathy, skill, and credibility.
